Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. # 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │

## Objective
- Build a playable 2D top-down house raid browser game where houses have at least 5 rooms and 1 hallway, armed men are stationary but fight back, and the player sees only a 45° cone with everything outside slightly blurry.

## Requirements
- 2D top-down perspective.
- Each house must have at least 5 rooms and at least 1 hallway.
- Armed enemies do not move but return fire.
- Player visibility limited to a 45-degree view cone; outside that area must appear slightly blurry.
- Game should be responsive and support mobile touch controls.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a static HTML/CSS/ES-module Canvas 2D game with no external dependencies.
- Procedural floorplan always generates 6 rooms + 1 central hallway.
- Vision cone is a true 45° total arc (`CONE_HALF = Math.PI / 8`), with raycast wall occlusion and a low-resolution upscaled blur layer outside the cone.
- Enemies are static, rotate/aim, use LOS, wind-up telegraphs, burst fire, and varied health.
- Added HUD, minimap, start/results/pause screens, synthesized WebAudio, desktop + touch twin-stick controls, debug hooks, and adaptive render scale.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `styles.css`, and modules `src/main.js`, `src/house.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/utils.js` created.
- Procedural house generation, furniture, walls/doors, enemy placement, collision/vision segments, and minimap/floorplan rendering implemented.
- Gameplay loop, shooting, enemy AI/fire, health/armor, reload, win/death states, results, pause, audio, touch controls, and debug API implemented.
- Start screen and in-game HUD visually verified via Playwright screenshots.
- Confirmed generated house data: 6 rooms, 1 hallway, 10 hostiles, 20 walls, 34 furniture items.
- Fixed several bugs: hall furniture null door clearance, zero-height partition walls, auto-reload logic, room-clear toast overwriting win toast, initial reticle positioning.
- Reduced blur cost using a downscaled blur canvas; removed expensive HUD `backdrop-filter`.

### Active
- Performance is still only ~6–15 FPS in the SwiftShader/Xvfb test environment.
- Added `?rs=<scale>` render-scale override and default `VIEW.rs = 0.7` for large screens; currently testing FPS at various render scales.
- Latest test run failed because `window.__IRONSIGHT__` was undefined, likely due to a JS initialization error after the render-scale edits.

### Blocked
- Need to fix the initialization/order bug causing `window.__IRONSIGHT__` to be undefined before further FPS/visual verification.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `src/main.js` top-level declaration order: `const RS_OVERRIDE = Number.parseFloat(QUERY.get('rs') || '')` references `QUERY` before `const QUERY = new URLSearchParams(...)` is declared, causing a temporal-dead-zone `ReferenceError`. Move `QUERY`/`DEBUG` declarations above `RS_OVERRIDE`.
2. Re-run `/tmp/opencode/perf3.mjs` to measure FPS at `rs=1`, `0.85`, `0.7`, `0.6`, `0.5`, then choose an adaptive/default render scale that keeps the game playable in software rendering without degrading normal GPU quality.
3. Re-run `/tmp/opencode/check.mjs` and inspect `screenshots/start.png`, `game.png`, `game-aim.png`, `game-move.png`; also take a fresh non-debug gameplay screenshot.
4. Brighten the scene: current gameplay is very dark, especially outside the cone. Reduce outside overlay (`rgba(3,7,11,0.4)`), raise floor/wall/furniture lighting, and strengthen lamp pools while preserving the blurred-outside effect.
5. Verify mechanics: move through rooms, shoot/kill enemies, confirm room-clear and win/death result screens, reload, pause, and mobile layout.
6. Add/adjust README documentation and remove or keep debug timing hooks as appropriate.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game shell, HUD, start/results/pause screens, touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: full visual design, responsive HUD, start screen, touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game state, input, combat, camera, vision/blur compositing, HUD updates, debug API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/house.js`: procedural 6-room + hallway generation, walls/doors/furniture/enemy placement.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: static world rendering, furniture art, lighting, minimap/floorplan/compass.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: synthesized WebAudio effects and ambient drone.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/utils.js`: math, RNG, raycasting, collision, formatting helpers.
- `/tmp/opencode/check.mjs`: Playwright screenshot/console verification script.
- `/tmp/opencode/debug.mjs`: debug house/game screenshot + house data verification.
- `/tmp/opencode/perf3.mjs`: render-scale FPS benchmark script.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: generated screenshots for visual review.

## Important Context
- Dev server is running in tmux session `ironsight` on `http://localhost:3002` using `PORT=3002 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`.
- Playwright test environment uses SwiftShader CPU rendering; ~48 FPS blank canvas, but current game canvas composition is much slower.
- `VIEW` currently: `{ w, h, dpr, zoom, rs }`; `rs` defaults to `0.7` when `w*h > 900000`, otherwise `1`; query `?rs=` overrides.
- Canvas internal resolution now uses `pixelScale = VIEW.dpr * VIEW.rs`; all drawing remains in CSS coordinates.
- Blur layer uses `blurCanvas` at `BLUR_SCALE = 0.42`, drawn upscaled; no expensive `ctx.filter` on the main canvas.
- Debug modes: `?debug=1` disables vision/blur compositing; `?debug=house` renders full house overview.
- Debug API `window.__IRONSIGHT__` exposes `state`, `house`, `world`, `view`, `camera`, `perf`, `startGame`, `retryHouse`, `startNewHouse`, `killAll()`, `clearRoom(id)`, `teleport(x,y)`, `aim(angle)`, `setGodMode(on)`.
- `setGodMode` is currently exposed but not wired into `damagePlayer`.
- Current start screen visual is good; gameplay is too dark and needs brightness/contrast tuning.
- Known latest error source: `RS_OVERRIDE` is declared before `QUERY` in `src/main.js`; this must be fixed first.
- No git commit/push has been made.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## IRONSIGHT — 45° house raid

A self-contained 2D top-down tactical shooter built with Canvas 2D and ES modules. No build step, no external dependencies.

You are the operator. A procedurally generated safehouse holds armed hostiles. You can only see a **45° cone** in front of you; everything outside it is rendered through a soft blur. Clear every room before the house clears you.

### Play

Open `index.html` through any static web server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
# then open http://localhost:3002
```

**Desktop:** `WASD` / arrow keys move · mouse aims · left mouse button fires · `R` reloads · `Esc` or `P` pauses.

**Mobile:** left stick moves · right stick aims and fires · the round button reloads · the pause icon opens the pause screen. The HUD and controls adapt to portrait and landscape safe areas.

### What is in the house

- Every generated house has **6 rooms plus a central hallway**, with doors, furniture, lamps and a minimap.
- **10 hostiles** are placed across the rooms and hallway. They never move, but they track the player, telegraph their shots, and fire bursts when they have line of sight.
- Walls and tall furniture occlude both vision and bullets. The sharp area is raycast from the player; the rest of the frame is a low-resolution blur layer.
- Health, armor, magazine/reserve ammo, reload timing, hit markers, room-clear callouts, mission results and a pause screen are all included.
- Synthesized WebAudio effects are generated at runtime; audio starts after the first user gesture.

### URL options

| Query | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `?seed=12345` | Reproduce a specific house layout. |
| `?rs=0.6` | Force a render scale between `0.4` and `1`. |
| `?debug=1` | Disable the cone/blur compositing for inspection. |
| `?debug=house` | Draw the whole floorplan with player/enemy markers. |

Render scale adapts automatically: `0.6` on software rasterizers (SwiftShader/llvmpipe), `0.7` on large screens, and `1` on smaller displays. The debug API is available at `window.__IRONSIGHT__` for scripted checks (`state`, `house`, `view`, `teleport`, `killAll`, `clearRoom`, `damage`, `setGodMode`, and more).

### Source layout

- `index.html` — game shell, HUD, screens and touch controls.
- `styles.css` — responsive layout, HUD and screen styling.
- `src/main.js` — game loop, input, combat, camera, vision/blur compositing.
- `src/house.js` — procedural floorplan, furniture, enemy and lamp placement.
- `src/world.js` — baked world rendering, lighting, minimap and floorplan.
- `src/audio.js` — synthesized sound effects and ambience.
- `src/utils.js` — math, RNG, raycasting and collision helpers.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable 2D top-down house raid browser game where houses have at least 5 rooms and 1 hallway, armed men are stationary but fight back, and the player sees only a 45° cone with everything outside slightly blurry.

## Requirements
- 2D top-down perspective.
- Each house must have at least 5 rooms and at least 1 hallway.
- Armed enemies do not move but return fire.
- Player visibility limited to a 45-degree view cone; outside that area must appear slightly blurry.
- Game should be responsive and support mobile touch controls.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/ES-module Canvas 2D game, no external dependencies.
- Procedural floorplan always generates 6 rooms + 1 central hallway.
- True 45° total arc (`CONE_HALF = Math.PI / 8`), raycast wall/tall-furniture occlusion, outside rendered via downscale/upscale blur layer.
- Enemies are static, aim/rotate, use LOS, wind-up telegraphs, burst fire, varied health.
- Enemies without vision LOS are not drawn, so they do not show through walls; blurred enemies remain visible through open sightlines.
- Vision compositing now renders the scene directly to the main canvas, then overlays blur/darkness only outside the cone via even-odd clip; removed the intermediate `sceneCanvas`.
- Pre-rendered radial sprite canvases replace per-frame full-screen radial gradients for cone fade and warm light.
- Software rasterizer detection (`swiftshader|llvmpipe|softpipe|software`) selects render scale `0.6`, blur scale `0.3`, and hides grain; hardware default remains `0.7` for large screens / `1` for small.
- Grain is static (no animation) and uses normal blending, improving software FPS.
- Mobile coarse layout separates top HUD, touch sticks, reload, and bottom HUD; duplicate touch pause button hidden; room chip moved below mission card in narrow portrait.
- Desktop and touch-specific start/pause hints added.
- Debug API retained and extended; `setGodMode` now wired to `damagePlayer`, and `damage(n)` added for scripted tests.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed temporal-dead-zone bug: `QUERY`/`DEBUG`/`DEBUG_HOUSE` now declared before `RS_OVERRIDE`.
- Fixed double camera transform that misaligned world rendering and vision cone.
- Fixed camera void/path cutoff by reverting to clamped camera bounds.
- Reduced blur cost, removed expensive `ctx.filter` blur, lowered blur scale.
- Rebuilt vision compositing to reduce full-screen passes; replaced gradient fills with cached sprites; cropped world draw to visible source region.
- Brightened scene: lamp intensity `0.16→0.23`, hall lamp `0.11→0.16`, outside overlay `0.4→0.3`, lighter CSS vignette.
- Added software-renderer detection and adaptive quality; grain hidden on software.
- Fixed mobile HUD overlaps, title overflow, duplicate pause button, joystick/panel collisions, reload overlap, toast positioning (`position: fixed`), and touch start hint spacing.
- Verified mechanics: movement, shooting/kills, ammo decrement, reload (`24/144 → 24/136`), pause/resume, win screen, retry, death screen, room-clear toast (`KITCHEN CLEAR`), new seed, and new house from pause.
- Verified touch controls: left-stick movement, right-stick aim/fire, touch reload, HUD pause.
- Verified 10 seeds all produce 6 rooms, 1 hallway, 10 hostiles, 20 walls, 6 doors, 34–40 furniture items, each room 1–2 enemies and hallway 2.
- Verified no console/page errors in desktop, mobile, touch, and flow tests.
- Added README game documentation and URL/debug options.
- Confirmed source syntax with `node --check` on all `src/*.js`.

### Active
- Final visual verification after latest vignette lightening and pause-hint changes.
- Performance remains ~8–13 FPS under SwiftShader/llvmpipe CPU rendering; JS frame work is <1 ms, raster/presentation dominates.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Re-run `/tmp/opencode/check.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/mobile.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/mobile-screens.mjs`, and `/tmp/opencode/playtest.mjs` after the latest CSS changes.
2. Inspect fresh `screenshots/start.png`, `game.png`, `mobile-start.png`, `mobile-portrait.png`, `mobile-landscape.png`, `mobile-pause.png`, and confirm the vignette brightness and pause hint text.
3. Consider whether the software fallback `VIEW.rs = 0.6` is acceptable or should be lowered to `0.55`/`0.5` for smoother CPU-only play.
4. Optionally remove unused `frameCount`, then finalize.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game shell, HUD, screens, touch controls, desktop/touch hints.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: HUD, start/results/pause screens, responsive coarse/mobile layout, vignette/grain.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game loop, input, combat, camera, vision/blur compositing, debug API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/house.js`: procedural 6-room + hallway generation, furniture/enemy/lamp placement.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: baked world rendering, lighting, minimap/floorplan/compass.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: synthesized WebAudio effects/ambience.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/utils.js`: math, RNG, raycasting, collision helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: game overview, controls, URL options, source layout.
- `/tmp/opencode/check.mjs`: desktop screenshot/console verification.
- `/tmp/opencode/playtest.mjs`: combat/reload/pause/win/death flow test.
- `/tmp/opencode/touchtest.mjs`: synthetic touch movement/aim/fire/reload/pause test.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile.mjs`: portrait/landscape mobile layout screenshots.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-screens.mjs`: mobile pause/win/dead screenshots.
- `/tmp/opencode/seeds.mjs`: multi-seed floorplan validation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: generated verification screenshots.

## Important Context
- Dev server is running in tmux session `ironsight` on `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright uses SwiftShader/llvmpipe CPU rendering; measured blank-canvas ~45 FPS, game ~8–13 FPS. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- `VIEW` is `{ w, h, dpr, zoom, rs }`; `rs` override via `?rs=0.4..1`; default `0.6` software / `0.7` large hardware / `1` small hardware.
- `BLUR_SCALE` is `0.3` on software, `0.35` otherwise.
- `drawScene(c, cam)` now accepts the target context and applies its own camera transform.
- Render order: scene → copy main canvas to blur canvas → even-odd clip outside cone → blur + dark overlay → clip inside cone → fade/light sprites → cone edges/reticle.
- Debug modes: `?debug=1` disables vision/blur compositing; `?debug=house` draws full floorplan overview.
- Debug API `window.__IRONSIGHT__` exposes `state`, `house`, `world`, `view`, `camera`, `perf`, `startGame`, `retryHouse`, `startNewHouse`, `prepareRun`, `killAll()`, `clearRoom(id)`, `teleport(x,y)`, `aim(angle)`, `damage(n)`, `setGodMode(on)`.
- Latest tests passed with no page errors; final screenshots after the vignette and pause-hint edits have not yet been captured.
- No git commit/push has been made; all game files remain untracked.
